A1.justification: Both complete, readable 33-page PDFs describe the same FusionFactory study. Main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices can be matched despite renaming and substantial rewriting.

before.justification: v1 reports original routing comparisons, thought-fusion experiments, fine-tuning results, and qualitative case studies, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds inference-time measurements and analysis of selected reasoning versus non-reasoning responses.

M1.justification: The reward-based routing, retrieved thought templates, and supervised distillation procedures remain unchanged in Equations 1–5. Renaming Top-K Router SFT to Top-K SFT and clarifying the overview do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions report the same 14 tasks across six domains and the same 20 LLMs. FusionBench becomes LLMFusionBench. QuAC's metrics row is removed, but neither version reports sample counts or experimental results for it.

E2.justification: The five evaluated routers, static baselines, prompting comparators, and label-only SFT baselines are retained. LLM-Blender and FuseLLM appear in v2's literature comparison, not as newly evaluated experimental baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds a full-test inference-time comparison using LLaMA-3 (8B) and domain-level measurement of response-style proportions under hybrid selection. Existing split sizes, routing reward weights, and fine-tuning budgets are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendices D and G analyze inference/retrieval overhead and the composition of hybrid-selected responses. The latter measures selection preferences rather than ablating reasoning data to measure accuracy effects. Existing sensitivity comparisons and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added mean latencies and selection percentages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Scores in Tables 4–6 and v1 Table 13/v2 Table 14 are unchanged. New Table 11 reports zero-shot/few-shot/thought-hybrid latencies of 3.74/3.89/3.91 seconds; Table 15 adds selection ratios. Section 5.3 incorrectly changes coding accuracies from 0.33 and 0.52 to 0.33% and 0.52%, despite unchanged Figure 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5 retain the same mathematical definitions and optimization objectives; changes to Reward arguments are notational. No new assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The benchmark, three-level framework, and principal performance claims remain. v2 adds explicit core requirements that practical fusion accommodate local/API serving and different pipeline stages, making these applicability claims more central.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning negligible retrieval overhead, serving constraints, and domain-dependent preference for reasoning responses. Section 3 clarifies model-level fusion as post-hoc training rather than v1's confusing final-response meta-selection account. Appendix A's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly identifies FAISS retrieval and explicitly documents offline template preparation and online lookup behavior. Existing hardware, LoRA settings, training details, and code/API access links are retained.

R1.justification: The introduction and Table 1 substantially reposition the work: comparison shifts from routing datasets' response patterns and size to fusion stages, API compatibility, and domain coverage. LLM-Blender, FuseLLM, and distillation/model-merging context are added, while RouterEval and several cost/retrieval references are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodological explanations, results discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten and condensed. Terminology changes from routing data/FusionBench to multi-LLM log data/LLMFusionBench, router descriptions move to Appendix C, and appendices are reorganized.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned, two supplementary tables are added, and captions, document styling, and table placement change. Figures 1–6 retain their underlying diagrams and plots; existing result and case-study tables are largely reformatted or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new timing evidence and FAISS/offline-template details improve assessment of practical overhead, while Section 3 clarifies distillation. These provide a limited net gain despite the introduced percentage typo in Section 5.3. Core accuracy evidence is unchanged, and the new selection-ratio analysis does not establish causal benefits from reasoning data.
